text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Wednesday:
- Swiss Minister Jean-Pascal Delamuraz was released from hospital on Tuesday after recuperating from a liver operation.
Delamuraz had cancer of the liver.
- Switzerland is suspending all diplomatic contacts with Bosnia Herzegovina.
- Switzerland is ranked as the 11th least corrupt country, according to Transparency International in Berlin. The firm ranked Nigeria as the most corrupt of countries.

- Union Bank of Switzerland's (UBS) first half results surpassed the expectations of most analysts. The bank reported a 67.4 percent jump in group profit to 1.8 billion Swiss francs. Swiss Bank Corporation (SBC) and Credit Suisse are also expected to soon post similar results.
- Swiss Minister Ruth Dreifuss opens this year's annual international film festival in Locarno tonight, which will take place until August 16th.
- Some 12,500 people sought asylum in Switzerland in the first six months of 1997, 30 percent more than in the same period the previous year.
- Swiss retail sales sank by 1.8 percent in June 1997 compared to a 2.8 percent rise in May 1997 and a three percent decline in June 1996.

- Swiss publishing company Ringier is planning to launch a popular bimonthly business magazine in Germany that is expected to be read by millions. The magazine will be based upon ZDF's "WiSo" TV programme.

- Life in Switzerland has become less expensive, according to a survey by the Corporate Resources Group in Geneva. Zurich and Geneva fell by 14 positions from last year's ranking. Tokyo is still considered the most expensive city in the world.
- Swiss textile exports to the U.S. rose by 22 million Swiss francs in the first half of 1997 thanks to the rise of the dollar.
